utterances.text: Did you have to undergo any operations as a result of the injuries you received in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What kind of operations?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: My first surgical intervention was in Croatia with respect to my teeth. Then in another country I had two other operations, once again dental ones, and another operation on my head.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What long-term effects, if any, have you suffered, physical, psychological, or emotional, as a result of what was done to you in Omarska and what you experienced there?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Well, I have serious difficulties. How shall I put it? I have received treatment from different psychiatrists, the treatment is still ongoing, and my situation is very serious. I still have this fear in me; it comes and goes, anxiety.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that you knew Kvocka, Radic, and Prcac before you went to Omarska and that you saw them in the Omarska camp. Do you believe you would be able to recognise them today?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you look around the courtroom and tell us if you see Kvocka in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I can see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us where he's seated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: He's sitting between Radic and the other one, the one with his hands like this, with a red pencil in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note a positive identification of Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated he was sitting next to Radic. From where you are seated, is Radic to his left or his right? I'm talking -- excuse me. To your left or your right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: On my left.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is Radic wearing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Well, he's got a blue suit and a tie. He's lost a little weight but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would note a positive identification of Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And Prcac, would you look around the courtroom and tell us if Prcac is present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: The one with the yellow tie.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is he seated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have to explain it rather than point. Where is he seated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Where over there? If you look at the direction you are pointing, there's the row where you identified Kvocka and Radic. Where is Prcac in relation to that row? Is he in the same row?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if you need to get up to have a good look, you may do so, because there are obstacles in your path.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: It's that man there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is he wearing? You mentioned a yellow tie. What is he wearing? What else?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: A suit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: What colour is the suit?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Light.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: The person that you are looking at, what facial hair, if any, does that person have?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: He hasn't got any facial hair.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would note a failure to identify Prcac.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. No. No. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Witness, that's fine. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would note a failure to identify Prcac.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: I've got everything mixed up now. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our objection is that the identification is over.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I have, indeed, made a ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is the cross-examination and the questions of Judges. Ms. Hollis already said that the identification is over, but if the witness wants to say something. There's no problem, Witness. Just a moment. We haven't finished yet, Witness. We're just going to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have concluded our direct examination. We would note for the record, however, that based on the discussions that we had yesterday in the Status Conference, the Prosecution has foregone questioning into various areas that would be relevant to the common or jurisdictional elements. Should that evidence become relevant to our case and necessary, the Prosecution would reserve the right to recall this witness for those purposes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Ms. Hollis. Witness, we are going to have a break until tomorrow, and tomorrow you will be answering questions by Defence lawyers. Mr. Krstan Simic will begin with the cross-examination. That's enough for today. We will be here tomorrow, at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 2.42 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of June, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
